svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Save a known-valid recovery point
Application server (TLS-APP01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.10
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-app01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
openssl s_client -connect 10.90.0.10:443 -servername app.example.mil -CAfile ~/tls-work/root.crt
-verify_return_error -verify_hostname app.example.mil < /dev/null
sudo sh -c 'test ! -e /root/tls-rollbacks/after-renewal.conf && cp -a /etc/nginx/conf.d/app-tls.conf
/root/tls-rollbacks/after-renewal.conf'
sudo systemctl stop check-app-tls.timer
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
The current endpoint verifies and the protected after-renewal.conf baseline exists.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. This final lab changes only TLS-APP01 on isolated VMnet6. Confirm Module 7’s v3 certificate still
verifies and presents the correct page.
2. Run the read-only TLS test first. Only after it succeeds, save after-renewal.conf once as the known-
valid v3 baseline.
3. The timer will intentionally fail while the fixture is active; temporarily stop it for this recorded
practice window. Do not change the system clock.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
